title: fix(cli): retire `objectui add` and `analyze`'s two flags, no-ops that exited 0; one enumeration pin over the built CLI's commands (objectui#11496)
body:
Fixes #11496

Clause-②: yes

## What

`objectui add COMPONENT` was declared ("Add a new component renderer to your project") and documented with an example. Its action printed "Feature not implemented yet.", wrote nothing and exited 0. Triage ruled it retired, with no placeholder (ruling comment `5958245941`, on the precedents `5955124315` and `5957399263`). The ruling also asked for a family close-out over every command and flag, plus one enumeration pin over the built CLI's commands. This PR:

- removes the `add` command from `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` and deletes `packages/cli/src/commands/add.ts`;
- retires `analyze --render-performance`, the one further no-op the close-out found, and `analyze --bundle-size` with it (see Contract notes). Their option lines go from `cli.ts`, and the placeholder function and the option plumbing go from `commands/analyze.ts`;
- drops the `add` section and the `analyze` flag table from `content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx`, replaces its stored command count with a pointer to `objectui --help`, and drops the `add` section from `packages/cli/README.md`;
- adds the pins in `packages/cli/src/__tests__/cli-bin.test.ts`, all run through the built `dist/cli.js`;
- adds `.changeset/11496-retire-cli-add.md` (`@object-ui/cli` `minor`, BREAKING banner, one FROM to TO line per retired surface, a Clause-② line).

No refusal code was needed. Measured on the BASE build before any edit: the program declares no default command, `allowUnknownOption`, `passThroughOptions` or `allowExcessArguments`. `objectui bogus` exits 1 with `error: unknown command 'bogus'`, and `objectui --bogus` exits 1 with `error: unknown option '--bogus'`. So commander's default refusal applies once a command or option is undeclared.

Serial: PR objectui#11495 (`generate --from`) landed as `1fe05ff37` before the first edit here. This branch was fast-forwarded onto it, so `1fe05ff37` is the base. `origin/main` has not moved since.

## Contract notes

- **The accept set narrows (Clause-② yes).** The published `objectui` bin refuses three surfaces it used to accept:
  - FROM `objectui add COMPONENT` (exit 0, nothing written) TO a non-zero exit with `error: unknown command 'add'`, nothing written.
  - FROM `objectui analyze --render-performance` (exit 0, fixed text) TO a non-zero exit with `error: unknown option '--render-performance'`.
  - FROM `objectui analyze --bundle-size` TO a non-zero exit with `error: unknown option '--bundle-size'`. The replacement is `objectui analyze`, which prints the same bundle report.

  There is no alias, no deprecation window and no silent accept.
- **Why `--bundle-size` goes too.** It only chose between the bundle report and the render section. With the render section retired, the flag would be declared, documented and read by nothing, which is why `generate --output` was retired. Keeping it would leave that defect in place, so it goes. This is a judgement on top of triage's ruling; it is raised as an open question in the dev report so the contract review can overturn it.
- **Unchanged.** `objectui analyze` with no flag prints the bundle-size report of `dist/` byte for byte as before, minus the fixed render section. Its help description is untouched. No exported symbol of `@object-ui/cli` moves: `cli.ts` is the bin entry, and `analyze` is not in the package's `exports` (`src/index.ts` exports `serve` and `init` only).
- **`validate` and `check` are not edited.** Draft PR objectui#11069 owns them. Both measured as working (table below). That PR also edits the README's `validate` section and the docs' `validate` / `check` sections. Those regions do not touch the ones edited here: four untouched README lines separate the nearest hunks.

## Family close-out: every command and flag `cli.ts` declares

One run per row in a fresh temp directory, on the built CLI (exit code, files written). The rows were measured on the build of `4abc0aafa`, which differs from base `1fe05ff37` only by `generate --from`, plus the post-fix build for the rows marked "after". The help texts are commander's. Placeholders are spelled in capitals, because GitHub strips angle-bracket shapes from a saved body.

| Surface | `--help` says | `cli.mdx` says | Built CLI, measured | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `-V, --version` | output the version number | (not listed) | prints `17.6.0`, exit 0 | works |
| `-h, --help` | display help for command | `npx @object-ui/cli --help` | usage plus the command list, exit 0 | works |
| `serve [schema]` | Start a development server with your JSON/YAML schema | legacy alias of `dev`, "same positional argument and `-p`/`-h` flags as `dev` (no `--no-open`)" | empty dir: exit 1, "Schema file not found: app.json". Real project (`app.json`, deps installed): HTTP 200 from the dev server | works |
| `serve -p, -h` | Port / Host | as `dev` | bound to the given port and host | works |
| `serve --no-open` | Do not open browser automatically | says `serve` has no such flag | honoured: no browser attempt with it; without it, the "could not open the browser automatically" line | works; the docs row is wrong (Acceptance notes) |
| `dev [schema]`, `-p`, `-h`, `--no-open` | Start development server (alias for serve) | as `--help` | empty dir: exit 1. Real project: HTTP 200, `--no-open` honoured | works |
| `build [schema]`, `-o, --out-dir`, `--clean` | Build application for production | as `--help` | empty dir: exit 1. Real project: wrote `out/index.html` and `out/assets/`, exit 0; `--clean` removed a sentinel file | works |
| `start`, `-p`, `-h`, `-d, --dir` | Start production server | as `--help` | empty dir: exit 1, "Build directory not found". Built `out/`: HTTP 200 on `/` and on a deep route (SPA fallback) | works |
| `init [name]`, `-t, --template` | Initialize a new Object UI application with sample schema | as `--help` | 13 files written, exit 0; `-t form` honoured; `-t nope` exits 1 | works (`-t nope` leaves an empty directory, Acceptance notes) |
| `lint`, `--fix` | Lint the generated application code | Lint the generated application code with ESLint | fresh dir: exit 1, "No Object UI application found". Past its precondition: ESLint finds no config, reported as "Linting found issues", exit 1 | partial: cannot succeed on the app `dev` generates |
| `test`, `-w`, `-c`, `--ui` | Run tests for the application | Run the application's tests with Vitest | fresh dir: exit 1. Past its precondition: "No test files found", reported as "Some tests failed", exit 1 | partial: cannot succeed on the app `dev` generates |
| `generate`/`g TYPE NAME` | Generate new resources (objects, pages, plugins) | as `--help` | `page`, `object`, `resource` and `plugin` each write their file, exit 0; an unknown type exits 1 | works |
| `doctor` | Diagnose and fix common issues | Diagnose common environment issues (Node version, deps, config sanity) | diagnoses deps, Tailwind and tsconfig; writes nothing; prints no Node line; exit 0 even with an error-level finding | partial: no "fix" half, no Node check |
| `add COMPONENT` | Add a new component renderer to your project | Add a new component renderer scaffold to your project | three lines, nothing written, exit 0. After: exit 1, `error: unknown command 'add'` | **no-op, retired here** |
| `studio` | Start the visual designer | Launch the visual designer (`@object-ui/plugin-designer`) against the local project | in an objectui checkout: starts `apps/console`'s Vite dev server (MSW mode) on its fixed port, not the local project. In a simulated published install: exit 1, "Console app not found in workspace" | partial |
| `check` | Advisory JSON file sweep; run objectui validate for a verdict | as `--help` | empty dir: tally, exit 0; one recognised file: tally, exit 0 | works (owned by objectui#11069, not edited) |
| `validate [schema]` | Validate a schema file against ObjectUI specifications | as `--help` | valid `app.json`: exit 0; missing file: exit 1 | works (owned by objectui#11069, not edited) |
| `create TYPE NAME` | Create new resources | Scaffold a new ObjectUI plugin via `@object-ui/create-plugin` | `create plugin my-widget`: exit 1, `Cannot find module` on a `create-plugin/dist/index.js` path, in the checkout and in a simulated published install; another type exits 1 | partial: never succeeds |
| `analyze` | Analyze application performance | Analyze the built application | with `dist/`: totals and the ten largest files; without: a warning, then "Analysis complete", exit 0 | works (exit 0 without `dist/`, Acceptance notes) |
| `analyze --bundle-size` | Analyze bundle size | Inspect bundle size | the same report as `analyze`, alone. After: exit 1, unknown option | **retired here** (see Contract notes) |
| `analyze --render-performance` | Analyze render performance | Inspect render performance | fixed text, byte for byte the same in an empty directory and in a built project with `dist/` (same md5); exit 0. After: exit 1, unknown option | **no-op, retired here** |
| `help [command]` | commander's built-in | (not listed) | works | works (commander) |

## Pins

All of them are in `cli-bin.test.ts` and run through the built `dist/cli.js`:

1. `--help` > `lists exactly the declared commands, no more and no fewer`. This is the enumeration pin. It parses the Commands section of the root `--help` and asserts that the names equal `SUBCOMMANDS`, in both directions and without duplicates. Its lit control: commander's own `help` entry is read as the last entry, which proves the parse reached the end of the section. It replaces a containment check that a retired command coming back would have passed.
2. `the retired add command is refused (objectui#11496)`: `add Input` in an empty temp directory exits non-zero, stderr names `unknown command 'add'`, and the directory stays empty. Its control: `g page Probe` in the same directory then exits 0 and writes `pages/probe.json`.
3. `analyze refuses its retired flags (objectui#11496)`: each flag exits non-zero naming itself as an unknown option, and writes nothing. The control: `analyze` with no flag over a planted `dist/` exits 0, prints the bundle report and the planted file, and prints no render section. `analyze --help` lists neither flag, with a lit control on its own usage line.

`SUBCOMMANDS` drops `add`, and the `analyze` row leaves the "exposes the documented flags" table.

## Reverse verification

Predictions were written down before each run. Every leg ran on final head `5e7b89431`, with the fix committed.

- **BASE leg.** `cli.ts`, `commands/analyze.ts` and `commands/add.ts` were checked out at base `1fe05ff37`, with the pins at HEAD. Each blob equalled its base blob: `ab22eb7e6fa6`, `7d9e7e3af440`, `b2fd2fcae3e9`. The CLI was rebuilt: dist markers `add=1`, `render-performance=1`. Predicted 6 red. Observed `Tests 6 failed | 41 passed (47)`: pin 1, pin 2, both flag refusals, the no-flag control (it printed the render section), and the `analyze --help` pin.
- **Restore 1.** `cli.ts` and `analyze.ts` blobs equal HEAD (`004165f17300`, `63659c0b30c9`), `add.ts` is absent, `git diff HEAD` is empty and `git status --porcelain` is empty.
- **Ablation.** objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` ran in wrap mode on the committed fix, with its restore trap. It planted back into `cli.ts` an `add` command that prints one line and exits 0, plus both `analyze` option lines; `analyze.ts` stayed fixed. Anchor `x1 -> x0`, blob `004165f17300 -> cdd4d9455089`. Source markers `add=1 render-perf=1 bundle=1`; the CLI was rebuilt; dist markers `add=1 render-perf=1 bundle=1`. Predicted 5 red, with the no-flag control staying green because `analyze.ts` was not mutated. Observed `Tests 5 failed | 42 passed (47)`, on exactly those five names.
- **Restore 2.** The tool restored through `git checkout HEAD --` on the absolute path. Blob after = HEAD blob `004165f17300`, `git diff HEAD` is empty and `git status --porcelain` is empty. CLI rebuilt; dist markers all 0; `Tests 47 passed (47)`.
- The same two legs ran once before, on `d9294d27b`, with identical counts. The only change since is reading the last `--help` entry by index rather than with `Array.at`.

## Tests and gates

All of these ran on final head `5e7b89431`.

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/cli build`: exit 0. `dist/` carries 0 hits each of `command("add")`, `render-performance` and `bundle-size`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/cli type-check` (`tsc --noEmit`): exit 0. `--listFiles` covers `cli.ts`, `commands/analyze.ts` and `cli-bin.test.ts`. An earlier run caught `Array.at`, which is not in this package's ES2020 lib; that is fixed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/cli/`, plus the cross-package readers of `cli.ts`, `cli.mdx`, the generator or the CLI bin: `toc-anchor-parity`, `nested-page-children-11223`, `page-node-headings-drawn-11436`, `body-dialect-census`, `filter-builder-mirror-6939`, `check-node-esm-load`, `one-authority-per-exported-name-6273`, `markdown-test-inputs`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`. Result: `Test Files 34 passed (34)`, `Tests 665 passed (665)`.
- The card's reproduction on the built CLI: `node packages/cli/dist/cli.js add Input` exits 1 with `error: unknown command 'add'`, and the directory stays empty.
- `pnpm docs:check-links`: `Links are valid across 17 scan roots.`
- `pnpm check:doc-fences`: ✅
- `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit`: `115 candidate test files, all adjudicated; 82 declared entries, all present.`
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`: ✅ OK
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only -> exit 0`
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: ✅. `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs`: ✅
- `pnpm check:changeset-claims` (report-only) names two pending changesets that mention a file this change touches. `7658-toc-code-span-anchor-parity` names `cli.mdx` and the README for the `add` heading its slug fix repaired; it is a past-tense account of that fix and is still true. `7694-chart-series-chart-type-alias-refusal` names `cli.ts` as the home of `objectui validate`, which is still true.
- `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:doc-types` and `check:doc-example-ids`: exit 0.
- **ESLint, as a proved narrowing.**
  - ① Population: CI lints this package through `turbo run lint`, which runs the package's `eslint src` against the root `eslint.config.js` (the package has no config of its own). I ran that same `eslint src`.
  - ② `--format json` counts 51 files linted, equal to the 51 tracked ts/js files under `packages/cli/src`. It reports 0 errors and 5 `no-explicit-any` warnings, all in untouched files. The three edited source files read 0/0.
  - ③ Invariance: the config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions` or `projectService`) and no import plugin, and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem. So this diff cannot move a verdict on a file it does not touch.
  - `cli.mdx`, the README and the changeset are outside every eslint `files` glob. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:doc-snippets` and `check:doc-examples`. Reason: PRECONDITION NOT MET (exit 2), because their scoped 34-package build was not run. The docs edit touches no ts or json fence; it removes one bash fence and one table. `check:readme-exports` is NOT MEASURED for the same reason (unbuilt packages); none of its unjudged lines is in `packages/cli/README.md`. The full `pnpm test` is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

Named here and not changed, per the close-out ruling (partials are named, never implemented).

- **`create plugin` never succeeds.** The script path is resolved one directory too high from the CLI's `dist/`: `../../../create-plugin/dist/index.js` lands on the repo root, or on a top-level `node_modules/create-plugin` in an install. `@object-ui/create-plugin` is not a dependency of `@object-ui/cli` either. Reported to the seat as a defect finding.
- **`lint` and `test` cannot succeed on the app `dev` generates.** The temp app declares neither ESLint nor Vitest and carries no config and no tests. The tool's own error is relabelled ("Linting found issues", "Some tests failed"). Measured past the precondition with a hand-built `.objectui-tmp`, not one a real `dev` run produced; said so in the report. Reported as a finding.
- **`studio`** runs the objectui console's dev server on its fixed port in a checkout, and refuses in a published install. The docs say it launches the designer against the local project. Reported as a finding.
- **`doctor`**: its help promises "fix", and nothing is written; its docs promise a Node version check, and none is printed; it exits 0 with an error-level finding.
- **`serve --no-open`** is declared and honoured, but the docs say `serve` has no such flag.
- **`analyze` without `dist/`** prints a warning and then "Analysis complete", exit 0.
- **`init -t nope`** refuses with exit 1 but leaves the empty project directory behind.
- **`dev` without `--no-open`**, where no browser opener exists, prints Vite's raw `spawn xdg-open ENOENT`; `serve` prints a readable line for the same case.
- **`toc-anchor-parity.test.tsx`** (`packages/plugin-markdown`) keeps an `add` heading row in `LIVE_SHAPES` whose `where` names `cli.mdx` and the README. That attribution is now stale; the row still exercises the slugger on its literal. It is outside this card's file surface.
- **The enumeration pin reads the built CLI only, not the docs.** Holding the docs' `### objectui NAME` headings to the same list from `cli-bin.test.ts` reds `markdown-test-inputs --audit` unless the test gains a row in that script's `ADJUDICATED` ledger. That file is outside this card's file surface, so the docs half is left to the seat (one ledger row plus about ten test lines). The `SUBCOMMANDS` comment says the docs headings are kept in step by hand.
